caption:
Two finals in two weeks for Lakshya Sen.

The eighth seed beat Indonesia's Alwi Farhan, the sixth seed and world No. 10, 21-12, 15-21, 21-11 in the Kumamoto Masters Japan semi-final today. He had lost both of their previous meetings.

Why it matters: only the top 8 qualify for the BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, and Lakshya was 12th in that race before this match. He already won the Hylo Open in Germany on Nov 1. Win Sunday's final against Kunlavut Vitidsarn or Koki Watanabe and it's back-to-back BWF Tour titles.

Can Lakshya make it two in a row? Tell us below.

Details via IANS, PTI and RevSportz.
